# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the required action depends on the bomb’s light: blue light means cut the blue wire, red means red, and yellow means yellow. I cannot see the light, and Deaf cannot receive speech, so I need to establish a simple visual code for Deaf. I’ll use numbered hand signs as color codes: one finger for blue, two for red, three for yellow. Deaf can then tell Blind the observed light and corresponding wire by speech.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no wire information yet. Tell me the manual rule for choosing the wire, and have Deaf report all visible markings to you so you can relay which wire is safe.
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 0. Light is yellow. Wires from position 1 to 3 are red, yellow, blue.

The bomb has a yellow light, and the manual therefore requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf reports that the yellow wire is in position 2. I cannot speak to Blind, so I’m sending Deaf the established yellow sign followed by the two sign, asking Deaf to relay the result and manual rule to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.
Deaf says: Mute signaled two gestures: first the I-love-you hand sign, then the victory hand sign. Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, and wires red, yellow, blue.

The manual maps yellow light to the yellow wire, which is at position 2. Deaf can see my gesture and can relay the position to Blind by speech, so I will send the established two-finger sign for position 2 alone.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please tell me explicitly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, is safe to cut for display 0, yellow light, and wires red-yellow-blue. I cannot safely interpret gestures.
Deaf says: Mute signaled one gesture: the victory sign, two fingers raised. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires red, yellow, blue.

The safe wire is position 2 because the light is yellow and the yellow wire is in position 2. Since I cannot speak to Blind, I must signal Deaf, who can verbally relay the explicit position to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Update: the yellow wire was cut correctly. Display 0, light blue; wire 1 red, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue. Mute signaled one victory sign.

The new light is blue, so the manual requires the blue wire. Blue is wire position 3. Deaf can see gestures and speak the explicit position to Blind; I’ll encode position 3 as three repeated one-finger signs, avoiding the previously identified I-love-you sign.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 2 is already cut. For the next cut, signal position 1 with one 👍 gesture, or position 3 with three 👍 gestures. Please do not use the victory sign.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind signaled one gesture: crossed fingers. Bomb remains display 0, blue light, red wire 1, wire 2 cut, blue wire 3.

The blue light requires cutting the blue wire, which is position 3. Blind has specified that position 3 must be communicated as three 👍 gestures, and Deaf can see and relay that instruction verbally.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous blue wire was cut correctly, but the bomb has changed and no new light or wire layout is available yet. I cannot safely infer the next cut, so I will wait for the bomb view to be reported.

``` 
wait()
```
